title: How To Be A Better, Calmer Teacher With Visualization ualization/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin describes a brief daily visualization practice, closing the classroom door, standing still, breathing, and mentally rehearsing the day, that he says makes teachers calmer and more effective from the very first use. He recommends visualizing three specific areas: the day's schedule unfolding smoothly, the teacher calmly following through on consequences like a referee even in worst-case scenarios, and specific lessons including introductions, modeling, and checks for understanding. He compares the practice directly to an athlete visualizing competition beforehand, arguing it primes the subconscious to handle situations more effortlessly when they actually occur. The article addresses the natural worry that visualization is one more item added to an already full plate, countering that the entire practice takes only a couple of minutes and gets faster with repetition. It closes by framing visualization as a low-cost, high-reliability way to improve teaching performance simply by mentally rehearsing success before it happens.

quotes: Daily visualization will make you a calmer, more effective teacher. And it works immediately.
Visualization is nothing more than seeing yourself performing your job well. Whatever you visualize tends to happen more effortlessly.
Here you’ll see yourself following through like a referee . Picture your most challenging class or difficult student and you fulfilling your promise calmly.

It’s no different than an athlete who visualizes their competition ahead of time, and just as effective. Whatever you rehearse in your mind’s eye will be easier and more effective when it comes to pass.
I can visualize my day in about 30 seconds and a lesson in half that time. It’s a fast-motion activity that very briefly touches on highlights and key areas.
